method.statistic: ratio of median completed-job times; includes initialization, encoder/filter drain, muxing and resource destruction
method.validation_outside_timing: every output decoded/count/PTS/GOP; last pair in each scene sampled at frames 0/900/1798; all five outputs per scene/backend are byte-identical
method.capture_and_validation_layers: disabled in medium-integrity ordinary user process (S-1-16-8192)
method.profiling: enabled in both paths; stage wall times overlap and must not be summed
method.cpu_pipeline: real CPU Renderer; three recycled BGRA buffers; raw channel capacity one; native AVFrame copy; CPU RGB overlay/NV12; hevc_nvenc p1 VBR hvc1
method.gpu_pipeline: real Vulkan Renderer; shared VkImages; libplacebo GPU NV12; hevc_vulkan VBR quality 0; synchronous initial PoC
method.scene_style: default ASS 720p font size 36, bold Microsoft YaHei, opacity 0.8
method.scene_content: synthetic 2 or 10 arrivals/sec, eight-second flights; rates are workload definitions, not scheduler defaults

limits: Generated background, no source-video decode, audio processing or project caches: do not treat this as a measured whole-project export ratio.
NVENC p1 and Vulkan quality 0 are backend-specific speed policies, not an equal-quality comparison; VBR actual bitrates differ.
CPU has observed hvc1, Vulkan has observed hev1; both have zero B-frames and GOP <=120.
Each job uses a new renderer and process. Warmups warm OS/driver caches; the CPU harness creates a small Tokio runtime whereas the application normally reuses it.
CPU readback is copying from a CPU Skia surface, not a measured PCIe GPU download. Vulkan removes this CPU full-frame path.
